content:
If you open Apple Maps today, you might notice that Apple has started renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America." The change comes in response to an executive order issued by Trump last week, incorporating the renaming into his ongoing trade dispute with Canada.

The change was first spotted by Bloomberg and applies to Apple Maps users in the United States. Apple Maps users in Canada will still see the name "Lake Ontario," while Apple Maps users elsewhere in the world will see both names.

Google Maps changed the name of Lake Ontario to "Lake America" a few days ago. At the time, Google said its policy is to follow the names designated by the U.S. Geographic Names Information System (GNIS).

U.S. Interior Secretary Doug Burgum said yesterday that Trump had "directly contacted Apple" to discuss the renaming. The conversation appears to have prompted Apple to follow suit and make the same change in Apple Maps.

Meanwhile, MapQuest announced this week that it was refusing to rename Lake Ontario to "Lake America," and the decision has driven a sharp increase in its downloads.

The change appears to be rolling out gradually to Apple Maps users. My own iPhone still shows "Lake Ontario," but some of the 9to5Mac team's devices are already seeing "Lake America."

Last year, when Trump ordered the Gulf of Mexico to be renamed the "Gulf of America," Apple similarly followed suit and made the change in Apple Maps.
